title: jwa-ajfa-world
label: Keith Wildwing

won.source: The fed's own served "And Justice For All" broadcast stages a twenty-man battle royal narrowing to a ladder match between Wildwing and Bryan Mercy for the vacant World Title; the surviving transcript cuts off before the finish, but "Blind Justice"'s own opening recap package confirms the outcome, showing Wildwing "his body tired and worn" holding "the JWA World Title loose in his hands."

how: Won the promotion's own inaugural World Title battle royal/ladder match at "And Justice For All."
note: The same "Blind Justice" recap frames Jon Clark as having then taken the title from Wildwing off-page, before Bryan Mercy won it in that same show's own main event — an intervening reign not structured here, since no document dates or stages it directly.

title: jwa-ajfa-world
label: Bryan Mercy

won.source: The fed's own served "Blind Justice" recap (not itself served) stages a Triple Threat Ladder Match in which "Mercy jumps and he makes it to the platform he has the belts."

how: Won a Triple Threat Ladder Match at "Blind Justice."
note: Confirmed still champion at "Dark Justice", successfully defending against War: "Your winner and still World Champion Bryan Mercy!!!" — the held record's latest dated title result.

title: jwa-ajfa-tv
label: Chad Hazzard

won.source: No document in the held record dates or stages Chad Hazzard's own title win; he is already champion, defending against Jose Gonzalez, when "Dark Justice" (14 November 1999) opens its own served part.

how: Unattested — the held record's only evidence is that Hazzard is champion by "Dark Justice."
note: Oasis is separately attested holding this title before this reign (billed defending against Gangrene at "And Justice For All," 22 August 1999) and Jose Gonzalez is billed at "Dark Justice" as "a former two-time JWA TV champion" — at least two intervening reigns (Oasis's loss, and both of Gonzalez's own reigns and losses) are implied but not dated or staged by any held document, so none is structured here.

title: jwa-ajfa-transatlantic
label: Matt Attict

won.source: No document in the held record dates or stages Matt Attict's own title win — the title was crowned in one of the five unserved parts of "And Justice For All" (22 August 1999) per that show's own opening promise. He is already champion, defending against Preacher, when "Dark Justice" (14 November 1999) opens its own served part.

how: Unattested — the held record's only evidence is that Attict is champion by "Dark Justice."
note: The title's own founding champion (crowned the night of "And Justice For All" per that show's own opening promise) is not named by any held document; Attict may or may not be that first champion.
